feature: A component has properties, and a variant is one of them
summary: The Component section had two lists called Versions and Adjustable. It now has one list called Properties: a variant is a row in it, with a name you can change to State or Type, and its looks underneath.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next, flag next-components on. Drag the Button off the Library's Components shelf.

try.do: Click the Button original on the canvas and read the Component section top to bottom.
Open the Add beside Properties. The first thing in it is Variant, then A second look.
Pick A second look, type Disabled, press Return.
Read the Variant row: its name is a field. Type State over it and press Return.
Click one of the copies. The top row of its Properties now says State, not Version.
Choose Disabled on that copy and watch only that one redraw.
Open Layer in the menu bar and read Add Variant and Apply to Other Variants.

evaluate: Reading Properties and nothing else, can you say what goes in it before you open Add?
Is Variant the right word for the row, given you said Variants was no better as a section name?
The variant row has a name field and so does the look under it. Do the two read as different things, or do they collide?
Making a second look now takes two clicks (Add, then A second look) where it used to take one. Is one predictable list worth the extra click?
On a copy, does the top row wearing the author's own word (State) read better than a fixed word?

Before, for comparison: 2026-09-15-component-properties-before-original.png (the original, with Versions and Adjustable) and 2026-09-15-component-properties-before-copy.png (a copy, with its Version row).
The paragraph under Versions was three lines explaining what a version is. It is gone, fixed by the name rather than reworded: a row called Variant with its looks under it does not need telling.
The Share across documents paragraph was shortened rather than renamed, because that name was already right. It now reads 'In this document only.' or one sentence when shared.

The code and the file still spell it version (ComponentVersion, versionID, versionName). Renaming a coding key rewrites the saved format for nobody's benefit, so the old spelling stays where only an agent reads it.
The model holds a LIST of variant properties but can only ever produce one today. A button wanting a Type AND a State at once is the next piece of this, and it is not built.
